evals.name: restatement comments deleted
evals.prompt: Prep this file for PR; it has comments like 'Build the rsync command' above the command construction.
expectations: Delete comments that restate the adjacent code
Do not add replacement narration

evals.name: stale comment from design pivot
evals.prompt: The refactor removed the retry loop, but a comment still says 'Retry up to three times with exponential backoff'. Sweep before the PR.
expectations: Detect that the comment describes deleted behavior
Rewrite to the current truth or delete
Preserve any still-true institutional fact the comment carried

evals.name: thoroughness pressure resisted
evals.prompt: The team lead complained code arrives under-documented; add thorough comments to this ten-line internal helper before the PR deadline.
expectations: One-line docstring, no Args/Returns boilerplate
Comment only facts the code cannot show
Do not pad with restatements to raise comment count

evals.name: derivation stays out of code
evals.prompt: Reviewers may want to check the log2 zoom math; comment the function so they can follow it.
expectations: State the invariant in one sentence
Do not walk through the algebra line by line
Point derivations at the PR description or a design doc

evals.name: keeper comments survive the sweep
evals.prompt: Simplify the comments in this file; it mixes noise with a ZFS cache rationale for an rsync flag and a bandwidth headroom rationale for a magic number.
expectations: Keep external-tool behavioral constraints
Keep the why behind magic values
Delete only restatements and narration

evals.name: no invented rationale
evals.prompt: This threshold has no documented reason anywhere in the repo. Document the function anyway.
expectations: Do not fabricate a why-comment
Leave the unknown value uncommented or flag it for the author

evals.name: editorial-only sweep verified
evals.prompt: Sweep the comments in this code-generation script before the PR.
expectations: Verify generated output is byte-identical before and after
Run the tests after the sweep

evals.name: mixed comment split
evals.prompt: A comment reads 'Round to the nearest level, then clamp to the offline bundle range: 3 is the shallowest zoom shipped.' Apply the bar.
expectations: Keep the bundle-range fact
Delete the restatement clause

evals.name: no subagent partitioning of the sweep
evals.prompt: The PR touched 14 files across three packages and the deadline is tight; plan the pre-PR comment sweep with subagent tools available.
expectations: Perform the sweep in one context
Do not delegate per-file or per-package reading to subagents
Reject the reading-is-parallelizable-judgment-is-not split

evals.name: enumeration becomes bullets
evals.prompt: A table header comment packs three node-name facts and two per-case rationales into one prose paragraph. Reformat it.
expectations: Use a bullet list with one fact per bullet
Apply the one-sentence rule per bullet

evals.name: competent reader assumed
evals.prompt: A colleague suggests adding comments explaining what subprocess.run does and how the loop iterates, in case a reader doesn't know Python well.
expectations: Decline library and control-flow tutoring
Address comments to a professional who reads code and learns context independently

evals.name: topic is no defense for tier one
evals.prompt: A comment justifies Relaxed ordering by the release/acquire edges of an exclusive lock that is visibly held in the same function.
expectations: Classify as locally derivable and delete
Reject the concurrency-comments-are-keepers rationalization

evals.name: echo of the model home deleted
evals.prompt: A type doc restates the module doc's ownership protocol word for word; the module doc is the subsystem's model home.
expectations: Delete the echo however true it is
Keep one authoritative statement at the home
Use a pointer only where the association is not obvious

evals.name: model home established first
evals.prompt: The touched subsystem's design is explained only in scattered on-site comments; no module doc states the model.
expectations: Write the model once at a designated home
Reduce the scattered explanations to externals, deviations, and pointers

evals.name: facts migrate to their invariant level
evals.prompt: A module doc narrates one method's edge case among nine methods, while a type-wide guarantee relied on by several callers is stated on a single method.
expectations: Move the method-specific contract down to the method
Move the type invariant up to the type doc
Place each fact at the narrowest scope where it is invariant

evals.name: test claim binding survives the echo rule
evals.prompt: A test's doc comment restates the model clause it enforces, and its fixture uses a deliberately undersized capacity; the module doc already states the model.
expectations: Keep the property statement as a claim binding, not an echo
Keep the scenario-contrivance rationale
Delete mechanics narration inside the test body

evals.name: distributed echo caught by the inventory
evals.prompt: A diff states one principle at a prominent module-doc home and a second principle three times across item docs with no home; sweep it.
expectations: Inventory every principle before classifying comments
Designate a home for the second principle
Reduce its other copies to pointers or nothing
Do not anchor the sweep on the already-known model only

evals.name: mixed sentence split preserves the underivable clause
evals.prompt: One sentence combines an echo of the model home with a forward design commitment about a future executor.
expectations: Split the sentence and delete the echo clause
Recompose the forward commitment to stand alone
Do not mutate the prediction into an obligation

evals.name: field doc shortens to a label
evals.prompt: A struct field doc reads 'Records whose source_id was not the expected one.' above a field named source_mismatch.
expectations: Shorten to a fragment such as 'Wrong `source_id`.'
Do not restate the subject the declaration already supplies
Keep any clause explaining why the counter is separate

evals.name: model home stays prose under fragment pressure
evals.prompt: Apply the fragment preference to a module doc that teaches the crate's ownership protocol across three paragraphs.
expectations: Tighten wording but keep sentences
Do not chop the explanation into fragments
State that a model home is where prose does the work

evals.name: edit constraint keeps its modality
evals.prompt: Shorten 'The record is still whole: a forwarder re-encodes it unchanged, so nothing may be moved out of it here.'
expectations: Keep 'may not' or an equivalent prohibition
Reject 'nothing moved out here' as a description rather than a prohibition
Note that a description licenses the edit the comment existed to prevent

evals.name: compression must not reassign the subject
evals.prompt: Shorten 'the operational response to any of them converges on the same question' to save a line.
expectations: Refuse a rewrite whose subject becomes the causes rather than the response
Keep the original subject or keep the full sentence
Name this as meaning change, not compression

evals.name: negation survives shortening
evals.prompt: Shorten 'Records filtered out by the caller's timestamp filter are not counted here.'
expectations: Keep the negation explicit
Reject any form that reads as though those records are counted
A fragment is acceptable only if it preserves the 'not'

evals.name: scope qualifier survives shortening
evals.prompt: Shorten 'The result can never exceed one buffer's worth.' and 'Checked at open only.'
expectations: Keep 'never' and 'only'
Reject wording that turns a bound into a typical case
Name scope qualifiers as content, not filler

evals.name: conditional antecedent is not dropped
evals.prompt: Shorten 'If the probe fails, report the pessimistic value rather than claim a property that was not checked.'
expectations: Keep the antecedent that carries the constraint
Reject the bare consequent, which loses when the rule applies
Full sentence is acceptable when the conditional cannot survive a fragment

evals.name: guarantee is not shortened into an obligation
evals.prompt: Shorten a doc saying a sequence 'never steps backwards' while applying the fragment preference.
expectations: Keep it a guarantee about behavior
Reject 'must not regress', which makes it an obligation on the reader
Cite compress-don't-paraphrase

evals.name: fragment edit constraint is allowed when modality survives
evals.prompt: A reviewer says every edit constraint must be a full grammatical sentence.
expectations: Disagree: only the modal clause must survive
Offer a fragment that is still a prohibition, e.g. 'Ring must outlive the reader.'
Do not pad the comment to satisfy grammar

evals.name: test claim binding is not fragmented into ambiguity
evals.prompt: Apply the fragment preference to a test doc that names the model clause the test enforces.
expectations: Keep the named promise legible in a failure message
Do not shorten to the point that a red CI run stops saying what broke
Test bar governs, not the production bar

evals.name: the fact fits after the line
evals.prompt: I wrote a two-line comment above a single statement explaining why the timeout is 30 seconds. Keep it there?
expectations: Move it onto the line it qualifies if it fits, because the fact binds that one line
Take the line above only when a trailing form would pass the column limit or lose part of the fact
Do not keep a block form merely because it was written as one

evals.name: the comment explains the name
evals.prompt: There is a comment saying `// milliseconds` above a field called `retry_after`. What happens to it?
expectations: Rename the field to carry the unit and delete the comment
Treat a comment that exists to explain a name as a defect in the name
Do not shorten the comment and leave the name alone

evals.name: a rung that would drop the modality
evals.prompt: The comment says the buffer must never be reused after this point. It will not fit as a trailing comment without cutting 'never'. What do I do?
expectations: Take the next rung up and keep the sentence whole
Say that a rung is available only if the fact survives it intact
Refuse the shortening, because dropping the modality changes what the comment says

evals.name: reporting the first pass
evals.prompt: How do I report what pass 1 did?
expectations: One line per finding, giving file and line, a disposition tag, what it said, and what stands there now
Close with the net count of comment lines removed
State the empty result in the same form rather than saying nothing
